title: Architecture: Repeatable De-Identification Pipeline Across 5 Datasets
brief: Strip direct and indirect identifiers across 5 datasets (internal Gmail logs, code repository, CRM lead records, email engagement metrics, and creator analytics) before partner sharing. Preserve analytical value via deterministic tokenization/hashing and k-anonymity rules, plus a validation report confirming re-identification checks return zero PII.
summary: Deterministic Python rules and HMAC-SHA256 tokenization scrub emails, phones, names, and company metadata across all 5 sources; NER/LLM assistance only flags free-text edge cases before a final automated re-identification test suite runs.

code: Deterministic regex + keyed HMAC-SHA256 pseudonymization per join key so CRM/email/creator analytics remain joinable without exposing names or emails
AST/comment & secret scrubbing pass on the code repository (git-filter/author rewriting + regex entropy checks)
Automated validation test suite checking direct PII patterns, rare quasi-identifier k-threshold, and schema integrity
ai: NER pass on unstructured Gmail thread bodies and CRM notes to surface contextual person/company mentions missed by regex
Residual-risk spot audit helper flagging indirect company references in free text before final export

milestones.deliverable: Audit all 5 input schemas, agree on join-key salt strategy, and run deterministic scrubber on a small sample drop
Repeatable Python + SQL scripts covering Gmail, code repo, CRM, email engagement, and creator metrics
Clean share-ready outputs, automated re-identification validation report, and rerun documentation

monthlyOps: Runs 100% offline/locally in Python on your own machine or VPC ($0 API cost required if using local NER + deterministic HMAC rules).
questions: Do datasets need consistent cross-table join keys (e.g., salted HMAC per creator/lead ID across CRM and email logs)?
What format is the Gmail export (MBOX, JSON, or API dump) and does the code repo need git commit history scrubbed too?
Are there minimum k-anonymity thresholds or specific regulatory rules (GDPR/DPDP) expected in the technical brief?
